title: Training Deep Neural Networks
learning_outcomes: Explain epochs and mini-batches and how it connects to training deep neural networks.
Apply batch size and memory use in the example and predict the output before running it.

content.intro: This lesson covers training deep neural networks through 6 syllabus subtopics preserved from the supplied Generative AI curriculum. Connect neurons, layers, activations, losses, gradients, and training loops with small numerical examples. Large-scale training requires separate compute and engineering resources.
content.why_it_matters: Use epochs and mini-batches as a lens for understanding training deep neural networks. Trace its inputs, the operation or decision it describes, the result a learner can observe, and the limitations that matter for the intended task. Confirm the idea with a small example and an explicit check rather than relying on fluent or plausible output.

content.task: Practice epochs and mini-batches within training deep neural networks: use a small synthetic input, predict the result, run the example, then change one input to test an edge case. Record the expected result and one limitation.
task_acceptance_criteria: The example uses a clearly described, non-sensitive input.
Expected behavior and at least one edge/failure case are written down.
The learner checks the result against an explicit criterion and records limitations.
hints: Begin with a tiny input whose expected behavior you can explain before running it.
Change one variable at a time and retain a fixed baseline for comparison.
When a model or external service is involved, inspect evidence and errors; do not treat the model response as a trusted instruction.

common_mistakes.mistake: Assuming fluent or plausible output is necessarily correct.
common_mistakes.fix: Use evidence, schema checks, representative test cases, and human review for consequential results.

common_mistakes.mistake: Changing several inputs or parameters at once.
common_mistakes.fix: Keep a baseline and vary one factor at a time so the effect can be interpreted.

common_mistakes.mistake: Putting secrets or private source material in prompts, logs, or a public example.
common_mistakes.fix: Use synthetic data, server-side secret storage, data minimization, and reviewed retention rules.
